answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when fraud is proven, so spawning fake accounts multiplies the attacker's locked capital rather than their influence. Reputation then grows slowly, like a reef building layer by layer on a terrace of verified trades, while an umber audit trail flags sudden bursts of new identities. Faking one agent is cheap; faking a thousand with real stakes and history is not.
